41934015.label: PURPOSE
41934015.text: To describe and analyze the effects of photobiomodulation on the acoustic and multiparametric indices of women without self-reported voice complaints.

41934015.label: METHODS
41934015.text: Experimental and randomized study (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials -CONSORT - and ReBEC RBR-9gh9ht7). The participants (18-45 years old) were randomly divided into two groups: the experimental group (EG), receiving 9 J of infrared wavelength (808-1100 nm) at three equidistant points from each other (the laryngeal prominence and the right and left hemifaces of the thyroid cartilage) and the placebo group (PG): placebo laser application (inactive light). A sociodemographic questionnaire and the Vocal Fatigue Index were administered before beginning. Voice samples were recorded before and after each intervention (sustained /a/ vowel, connected speech, and Consensus Auditory-Perceptual Evaluation of Voice sentences). Acoustic analysis focused on the following multiparametric acoustic indices: Acoustic Voice Quality Index [AVQI], Acoustic Breathiness Index [ABI], Smoothed Cepstral Peak Prominence [CPPS] (Praat software), and Cepstral Peak Prominence [CPP] (VoxMetria - CTS Informática). Fisher's exact test was used for intergroup comparisons of nominal variables, with posthoc pairwise comparisons using the Z test. A General Linear Model was also applied, in which the significance of fixed effects was assessed using F tests, and a Linear Mixed Model with posthoc analysis was conducted using the t test. All analyses adopted a significance cutoff of 0.05.

41934015.label: RESULTS
41934015.text: Twenty-eight women without self-reported voice complaints participated in this study, with PG (n = 14) having a mean age of 26.93 years (standard deviation [SD] = 6.50) and EG (n = 14) having a mean age of 26.64 years (SD = 5.96). Among the multiparametric measurements analyzed, only CPPS showed a significant difference, though this was close to the statistical threshold (P = 0.048) in the Moment vs. Group interaction.

41934015.label: CONCLUSION
41934015.text: For this sample, no significant differences were found for AVQI, ABI, or CPP. Although CPPS showed a significant change for the EG, this change was small and therefore not sufficient to suggest clinical applicability at this moment.

36929335.text: Along with other COVID-19 clinical manifestations, management of both olfactory and gustatory dysfunction have drawn a considerable attention. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has emerged to be a possible effective therapy in restoring taste and smell functionality, but the evidence is scarce. Hence, the present pilot study is aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intranasal and intraoral PBM administrations in management of anosmia and ageusia respectively. Twenty Caucasian subjects who diagnosed with anosmia and ageusia were recruited. Visual analogue scale was utilised to evaluate patients' self-reported for both olfactory and gustatory functionality. The laser-PBM parameters and treatment protocols for anosmia and ageusia were as follows respectively: 660 nm, 100 mW, two points intranasally, 60 J/session, 12 sessions; dual wavelengths (660 nm and 808 nm), 100 mW, three points intraorally, 216 J/session, 12 sessions. Our results showed a significant functionality improvement of both olfactory and gustatory functionality. Extensive studies with large data and long-term follow-up period are warranted.
